UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Represents a user's profile within the Home Run Hub application, storing their identity and assigned role.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity. This typically corresponds to the Firebase Authentication UID.

email.description: The user's email address, primarily used for authentication and contact.

role.description: The user's assigned role within the application (e.g., 'Parent', 'Coach', 'Admin').

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the user profile was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the user profile was last updated.

Player.title: Player
Player.description: Represents a player managed by a parent, including personal details and linked documents.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Player entity.

parentUserId.description: Reference to the UserProfile of the parent who manages this player. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Player)

piaaClearanceDocumentPath.description: Firebase Storage path to the player's PIAA clearance document, if applicable.

birthCertificateDocumentPath.description: Firebase Storage path to the player's birth certificate document, if applicable.

Season.title: Season
Season.description: Defines a specific playing season, including its duration and registration periods.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Season entity.

startDate.description: The official start date of the season.

endDate.description: The official end date of the season.

registrationOpenDate.description: The date when registration for this season opens.

registrationCloseDate.description: The date when registration for this season closes.

Division.title: Division
Division.description: Represents a specific playing division within a season, including its name and associated registration fee.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Division entity.

name.description: The name of the division (e.g., 'T-Ball', 'Coach Pitch').

seasonId.description: Reference to the Season this division belongs to. (Relationship: Season 1:N Division)

feeAmount.description: The registration fee amount for this division, typically in the smallest currency unit (e.g., cents).

Enrollment.title: Enrollment
Enrollment.description: Records a player's enrollment in a specific season and division, along with payment status and details.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Enrollment entity.

playerId.description: Reference to the Player being enrolled. (Relationship: Player 1:N Enrollment)

seasonId.description: Reference to the Season the player is enrolling in. (Relationship: Season 1:N Enrollment)

divisionId.description: Reference to the Division the player is enrolling in. (Relationship: Division 1:N Enrollment)

parentUserId.description: Reference to the UserProfile of the parent who initiated the enrollment. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Enrollment)

paymentStatus.description: The current payment status of the enrollment ('pending', 'paid', 'failed').

stripeCheckoutSessionId.description: The ID of the associated Stripe Checkout Session.

registrationFeeAmount.description: The actual registration fee amount charged for this enrollment.

enrollmentDate.description: Timestamp when the enrollment was created.

Team.title: Team
Team.description: Represents a specific sports team within a season and division.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Team entity.

name.description: The name of the team (e.g., 'Red Rockets').

seasonId.description: Reference to the Season the team belongs to. (Relationship: Season 1:N Team)

divisionId.description: Reference to the Division the team plays in. (Relationship: Division 1:N Team)

coachUserId.description: Reference to the UserProfile of the coach assigned to this team. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Team)

playerIds.description: An array of IDs referencing the Players on this team. (Relationship: Player N:N Team)

Game.title: Game
Game.description: Represents a scheduled game or practice event for a team.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Game entity.

teamId.description: Reference to the Team participating in this game/event. (Relationship: Team 1:N Game)

opponentName.description: The name of the opposing team (for 'Game' type events).

location.description: The location where the game/event will take place.

dateTime.description: The date and time of the game/event.

description.description: An optional description or notes for the game/event.

RSVP.title: RSVP
RSVP.description: Records a parent's response to a player's availability for a specific game or event.

id.description: Unique identifier for the RSVP entity.

gameId.description: Reference to the Game or event the RSVP is for. (Relationship: Game 1:N RSVP)

playerId.description: Reference to the Player whose attendance is being confirmed. (Relationship: Player 1:N RSVP)

parentUserId.description: Reference to the UserProfile of the parent who submitted this RSVP. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N RSVP)

status.description: The player's attendance status for the event ('Attending', 'Not Attending', 'Maybe').

timestamp.description: Timestamp when the RSVP was submitted or last updated.

Message.title: Message
Message.description: Represents a message sent within a team's real-time chat or as a broadcast notification.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Message entity.

teamId.description: Reference to the Team the message belongs to. (Relationship: Team 1:N Message)

senderUserId.description: Reference to the UserProfile of the sender. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Message)

content.description: The textual content of the message.

timestamp.description: Timestamp when the message was sent.

Drill.title: Drill
Drill.description: Represents a practice drill suggestion, potentially generated by AI or created by a coach.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Drill entity.

name.description: The name of the practice drill.

description.description: A brief description of what the drill entails.

instructions.description: Detailed step-by-step instructions on how to perform the drill.

creatorUserId.description: Reference to the UserProfile of the coach who created this drill. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Drill)

ageGroup.description: The target age group for which this drill is suitable (e.g., 'U8', 'U10', 'High School').

skillLevel.description: The target skill level for players (e.g., 'Beginner', 'Intermediate', 'Advanced').

practiceFocus.description: The primary area of focus for this drill (e.g., 'Hitting', 'Fielding', 'Pitching', 'Teamwork').

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the drill was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the drill was last updated.

definition.description: Stores user authentication details and assigned roles. The `userId` parameter directly corresponds to the Firebase Authentication UID. The 'role' field is critical for DBAC.

params.name: divisionId

params.name: teamId
params.description: The unique identifier for the team.

Includes `parentUserId` (owner of the RSVP), `playerId`. **Includes denormalized `teamId`, `coachUserId`, and `parentUserIds` (from the parent Team document via the Game) for authorization independence, allowing coaches to view all RSVPs for their games and parents to manage their own.**

params.description: The unique identifier of the parent team.

params.name: gameId
params.description: The unique identifier of the parent game or event.

params.description: The unique identifier for the RSVP.

Includes `senderUserId` (message author). **Includes denormalized `teamId`, `coachUserId`, and `parentUserIds` (from the parent Team document) for authorization independence, ensuring only team members can read/write.**

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure for Home Run Hub prioritizes security, scalability, and debuggability by strictly adhering to the core design principles, especially Authorization Independence and Structural Segregation.

**Authorization Independence via Denormalization:**
This is achieved by strategically denormalizing authorization-relevant fields directly into the documents that require access control. This eliminates the need for expensive and complex `get()` calls in Firestore Security Rules, enabling atomic operations and simplifying rule logic. For instance:
*   **Player & Enrollment Documents:** `parentUserId` is stored directly in the document and matches the `{parentUserId}` wildcard in their respective paths (`/userProfiles/{parentUserId}/players/{playerId}` and `/userProfiles/{parentUserId}/enrollments/{enrollmentId}`). This allows rules to check `request.auth.uid == resource.data.parentUserId` or `request.auth.uid == parentUserId` directly, without looking up the parent's profile.
*   **Team, Game, RSVP, and Message Documents:** For collaborative entities, `coachUserId` and a denormalized list of `parentUserIds` (representing all parents of players on the team) are embedded within each `Team` document. Crucially, these `coachUserId` and `parentUserIds` are further denormalized into `Game`, `RSVP`, and `Message` documents. This allows security rules to instantly determine if `request.auth.uid` is the coach or a parent associated with the team, game, or message, fulfilling the "Membership Map" strategy for collaborative data. This ensures that rules like `request.auth.uid == resource.data.coachUserId || request.auth.uid in resource.data.parentUserIds` can be evaluated locally without cross-document reads.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters) and Structural Segregation:**

1.  **User-Owned Data:** User-specific data like `Player` profiles and `Enrollments` are nested under `/userProfiles/{userId}/...`. This structural segregation ensures that `list` operations (queries) for a parent's children or enrollments automatically apply the `parentUserId` filter, making rules simple (`allow list: if request.auth.uid == parentUserId;`). This ensures QAPs as only the authenticated user's data is returned.
2.  **Global Data:** `Seasons` and `Divisions` are placed in root-level collections (`/seasons/{seasonId}`, `/seasons/{seasonId}/divisions/{divisionId}`). These are generally public (read-only for all authenticated users) and admin-writeable. This segregation clearly defines their homogenous security posture.
3.  **Collaborative (Team-Scoped) Data:** `Teams` are at a root level (`/teams/{teamId}`), while `Games`, `Messages`, and `RSVPs` are subcollections (`/teams/{teamId}/games/{gameId}/...`). This grouping ensures that `list` operations for a team's schedule (`/teams/{teamId}/games`) or chat (`/teams/{teamId}/messages`) are naturally scoped to a specific team, and the denormalized `coachUserId` and `parentUserIds` in these documents allow rules to enforce team-specific access checks (`allow list: if request.auth.uid == teamId.coachUserId || request.auth.uid in teamId.parentUserIds;`). For RSVPs, parents can perform a collection group query on `rsvps` filtered by their `parentUserId`, which is supported by the denormalized `parentUserId` in the RSVP document.
4.  **Drills:** Drills are placed in a root-level `/drills/{drillId}` collection. While created by coaches, they are assumed to be broadly accessible for reading, with write access restricted to the `creatorUserId` or admin. This allows for QAPs for listing all drills, or filtering by `creatorUserId` for coaches to manage their own.

This design leverages explicit data ownership through path-based authorization and denormalized membership lists, enabling clear, concise, and performant security rules that inherently support QAPs by aligning data structure with access patterns.
